B. Is this measure already running in Central Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county (or in the OYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated. Every stage I patient who is too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy (3-8 visits, no anaesthesia) instead of being left without treatment. The treatment exists in every university hospital; what is missing in some counties is the referral rule.
effect_summary_en: Across the Netherlands, 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated once stereotactic radiotherapy (SABR) was fully available. That is the size among elderly stage I patients only, not among all lung cancer patients.
supported_en: A Dutch population study of 4605 patients (Annals of Oncology 2012) found a 7% absolute fall in untreated elderly stage I patients after stereotactic radiotherapy became available.
not_supported_en: The pages do not show the 0.8-point gain in the share of all patients treated with curative intent, or any figure for Finland or for Soite.
in_use_quote: Paikallisessa tai paikallisesti edenneessä taudissa, jos leikkaushoito ei ole mahdollista, voidaan antaa täsmäsädehoitoa tai yhtä aikaa säde- ja solunsalpaajahoitoa eli kemosädehoitoa.
missing_en: No page shows a written rule that every frail stage I patient from Soite is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy.
summary_en: OYS's lung cancer care-pathway page says that when surgery is not possible in local disease, precision radiotherapy ('täsmäsädehoito') can be given. It also says the university hospital runs the lung cancer team meetings and gives surgery and radiotherapy for the area. No page shows a rule that every inoperable stage I patient is referred. A Dutch national registry study (Annals of Oncology 2012) found 7% fewer untreated elderly stage I patients once stereotactic radiotherapy was available. This supports the direction of our assumption, but the step to a share of all patients rests on our own 8% assumption.
unanswered_en: I found no Soite page on stereotactic radiotherapy or its referral practice, and no Finnish data on how many stage I patients go untreated.
